# Edward Rothwell (engineer)

Edward Joseph Rothwell III (born 1957 in Grand Rapids, Michigan) is an American electrical engineer and Professor Emeritus at Michigan State University. He is a Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) for his contributions to electromagnetics, particularly in antenna design and electromagnetic scattering.
Education and career
Rothwell received an A.S. from Grand Rapids Community College in 1977, a B.S. in electrical engineering from Michigan Technological University in 1979, an M.S. in electrical engineering from Stanford University in 1980, an Engineer's degree from Stanford in 1982, and a Ph.D. in electrical engineering from Michigan State University (MSU) in 1985 under Kun-Mu Chen.
Before joining MSU, Rothwell worked at Raytheon from 1979 to 1982 on low power traveling-wave tubes and at MIT Lincoln Laboratory in 1985. He joined Michigan State University as an assistant professor in 1985, became an associate professor in 1990, and a full professor in 1998. He currently holds the Dennis P. Nyquist Professorship in Electromagnetics and is Professor Emeritus.
Rothwell is a member of the Electromagnetics Research Group at MSU and conducts research in antennas, electromagnetic scattering, radar target identification, electromagnetic theory, and electromagnetic measurements.
Books
Rothwell is co-author of three textbooks with Michael J. Cloud:
* Electromagnetics (CRC Press, 2001; 3rd edition 2018)
* Engineering Writing by Design: Creating Formal Documents of Lasting Value (CRC Press, 2014; 2nd edition 2020)
* Engineering Speaking by Design: Delivering Technical Presentations with Real Impact (CRC Press, 2015)
Awards and honors
* Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
* Dennis P. Nyquist Professorship in Electromagnetics, Michigan State University
* John D. Withrow Teaching Excellence Award, MSU College of Engineering (1991, 1996, 2006)
* MSU Alumni Club of Mid-Michigan Quality in Undergraduate Teaching Award, 2003
* Best Technical Paper Award, Antenna Measurement Techniques Association Symposium, 2003 (joint recipient)
* Southeast Michigan IEEE Section Award for Most Outstanding Professional, 2005
* Withrow Distinguished Scholar Award, MSU College of Engineering, 2007
